articles.name: Why is the "Closed" ticket status missing from my tickets?
articles.title: Why is the "Closed" ticket status missing from my tickets?
articles.body:
Question

Why do my closed tickets show a solved ticket status? When I check a closed ticket, I don't see the Closed status label.

Answer

When custom ticket statuses are activated, closed tickets retain the Solved category status with which they were solved. The tickets are still in the Closed state.

To learn more, see these articles:

  • Solving tickets with a custom status
  • Modifying closed tickets
  • What is the difference between a solved ticket and a closed ticket?

articles.name: Replacing legacy ticket creation workflows with AI agent tickets
articles.title: Replacing legacy ticket creation workflows with AI agent tickets
articles.body:
TheAI agent ticketsfeature automatically creates a ticket at the start of every AI agent conversation. That ticket is used to keep all context, outcomes, and reporting about the conversation in one place.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

The AI agent tickets feature automatically creates a ticket at the start of every AI agent conversation. That ticket is used to keep all context, outcomes, and reporting about the conversation in one place.

Prior to the introduction of the AI agent tickets feature, there was no standard way to create a ticket for an AI agent conversation. As a workaround, you may have previously set up one or more or the following workflows to create a ticket to record an AI agent conversation:

  • A configured action using the Create ticket action
  • An API integration using the Create Ticket API
  • The “Send an email” option of an Escalation block in a dialogue

These workflows were often configured to run when an AI agent conversation ended, and either created or updated a ticket in order to:

  • Escalate AI agent conversations as tickets instead of messaging conversations
  • Log AI agent conversations for reporting
  • Set ticket fields via an action or API payload

With the introduction of AI agent tickets, these workflows are considered legacy and will result in duplicate tickets if they run after the AI agent tickets feature is turned on in your account:

  • Ticket 1: Created automatically by the AI agent tickets feature when the AI agent conversation starts.
  • Ticket 2: Created by your legacy workflow at either the end of the conversation or during escalation.

The result is two tickets for one customer issue, leading to split context, a confusing agent experience, and inconsistent reporting. To eliminate the possibility of duplicate tickets, update any legacy ticket creation workflows you previously created as part of your escalation flows.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Before you start: A note about asynchronous ticket escalations
  • Identifying legacy ticket creation workflows
  • Updating escalation flows that use the Create ticket action
  • Updating escalation flows that use an API integration
  • Updating escalation flows that use the “Send an email” option
  • Testing your updates

Before you start: A note about asynchronous ticket escalations

Escalation flows can be either real-time, meaning customers are immediately transferred from your AI agent to a human agent, or asynchronous, meaning customers can leave messages when a human agent is unavailable. Regardless of whether your escalation flows are real-time or asynchronous, you need to follow the guidance in this article to update any legacy ticket creation workflows.

However, if you’ve configured asynchronous escalations, you should also follow the steps in Workflow recipe: Configuring asynchronous ticket escalations for messaging AI agents.

The goal with asynchronous escalations is to have one ticket for each AI agent conversation, while ensuring out-of-hours requests don’t sit in a live messaging queue or skew live-chat metrics. This applies to any availability-based escalation where live messaging is unavailable, undesirable, or an asynchronous Zendesk ticket is preferred.

Identifying legacy ticket creation workflows

As you get started with identifying any legacy ticket creation workflows, you may find it useful to create a spreadsheet to track your updates. Start by listing all of your AI agents, visible on the dashboard in the AI agents workspace. For each AI agent, record its associated escalation-related configuration, discussed below.

First, check whether you’ve created a configured action or API integration that creates a ticket. These configured actions and API integrations can be reused across dialogues. To review your:

  • Configured actions:
    1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
    2. Click Actions in the sidebar, then select Configured actions.
    3. Click each configured action to open its details to see whether it contains the Create ticket action.
    4. If it does, note this configured action in your tracking spreadsheet.
  • API integrations:
    1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
    2. Click Actions in the sidebar, then select API integrations.
    3. Click each API integration to open its details and see whether it uses the Create Ticket API.
    4. If it does, note this API integration in your tracking spreadsheet.

Next, identify all escalation flows you may have configured in your AI agent. Escalation flows can be configured as part of the Escalation reply system reply, dialogues, or templates. To review your:

  • Escalation reply:
    1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
    2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Use cases.
    3. Click the Categories filter, select System replies, and click Apply.
    4. Find the one called Escalation reply and review its associated dialogue to look for:
      • Any configured actions you noted above that use the Create ticket action
      • Any API integrations you noted above that use the Create Ticket API
      • An Escalation block with the “Send an email” option
    5. Note your findings in your tracking spreadsheet.
  • Dialogues:
    1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
    2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Use cases.
    3. For any use case that has a Reply method of Dialogue, open the associated dialogue and look for:
      • Any configured actions you noted above that use the Create ticket action
      • Any API integrations you noted above that use the Create Ticket API
      • An Escalation block with the “Send an email” option
    4. For any dialogues that contain any of the above, note your findings in your tracking spreadsheet.
  • Templates:
    1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
    2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Templates.
    3. For each template, open its associated dialogue in the Replies column and look for:
      • Any configured actions you noted above that use the Create ticket action
      • An API integrations you noted above that use the Create Ticket API
      • An Escalation block with the “Send an email” option
    4. For any templates that contain any of the above, note your findings in your tracking spreadsheet.

At this point, review your tracking spreadsheet and answer the following questions for each of the escalation flows you recorded:

  • Does this escalation flow use the Create ticket action?
    • Yes: See Updating escalation flows that use the Create ticket action.
    • No: Continue reading.
  • Does this escalation flow use an API integration that creates Zendesk tickets?
    • Yes: See Updating escalation flows that use an API integration.
    • No: Continue reading.
  • Does this escalation flow use the “Send an email” option in an Escalation in a dialogue?
    • Yes: See Updating escalation flows that use the “Send an email” option.
    • No: If you don’t use any of the legacy ticket creation workflows listed above and you still see duplicate tickets for AI agent conversations, you may have a custom setup (for example, triggers or external workflows creating tickets). Contact Zendesk customer support for further assistance.

Updating escalation flows that use the Create ticket action

If any of your escalation flows include a configured action that uses the Create ticket action, update or remove this configured action, as it’s no longer necessary with the AI agent tickets feature.

This section also applies to AI agent–level actions that are executed in every conversation your AI agent engages in, even if they’re not specifically added in a dialogue.

To update escalation flows that use the Create ticket action

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Actions in the sidebar, then select Configured actions.
  3. Find the configured action that uses the Create ticket action and do either of the following:
    • If the configured action includes other actions besides Create ticket (such as adding tags, custom fields, or routing information), edit it to remove the Create ticket action while leaving the other actions.
      Tip: If these actions should be applied to every escalation, make sure you’re using an AI agent–level action.
    • If the configured action includes only the Create ticket action, delete it.
  4. Test your updates.

Updating escalation flows that use an API integration

If any of your escalation flows include an API integration that uses the Create Ticket API, update or remove this API integration, as it’s no longer necessary with the AI agent tickets feature.

Note that there is an exception to this guidance: You may still need the API integration if you’re creating tickets in another Zendesk instance (cross-instance routing).

To update escalation flows that use an API integration

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Actions in the sidebar, then select API integrations.
  3. Find the API integration that uses the Create Ticket API and open it for editing.
  4. (Optional) If the API integration includes other actions besides creating a ticket, such as passing fields or tags information, create and add a configured action to pass that information instead.
    Tip: If these actions should be applied to every escalation, make sure you’re using an AI agent–level action.
  5. Delete the API integration.
  6. Test your updates.

Updating escalation flows that use the “Send an email” option

If any of your escalation flows include an Escalation block with the “Send an email” option, update the option to “Forward to agent” instead.

To update escalation flows that use the “Send an email” option

  1. Open a dialogue that includes an Escalation block that uses the “Send an email” option.
  2. In the Escalation block, click Send an email and select Forward to an agent instead.
  3. (Optional) If the goal of your original configuration was to notify another team or external party, also use action flows, side conversations, or a similar workflow automation to handle the notification.
  4. Test your updates.

Testing your updates

After making your updates, test the end-to-end customer experience to ensure the conversational experience, ticket routing, and reporting all work as expected. For help, see the following testing resources:

  • Testing conversation flows in AI agents
  • Best practices for testing AI agents

Additionally, make sure you understand the AI agent ticket experience so you know what the expected behavior is:

  • Understanding AI agent tickets for AI agent–only conversations
  • Finding AI agent tickets in your account
  • Interacting with AI agent tickets

As part of your tests, make sure you include the following:

  • AI agent conversations that resolve without escalation. You should see one AI agent ticket, and it should have a status of Solved.
    Note: Previously, the legacy ticket creation workflows may have assigned the tickets to a group, even for AI agent–resolved conversations. With AI agent tickets, AI agent–resolved tickets aren’t assigned to anyone, because no handoff occurred. This is expected behavior.
  • AI agent conversations that result in escalation. You should see one editable ticket that a human agent can work.

In both scenarios, validate that the ticket contains any updated fields or tags added by your configured actions, if applicable.

articles.name: Announcing AND/OR conditions and condition grouping in action builder
articles.title: Announcing AND/OR conditions and condition grouping in action builder
articles.body:
Action builder is introducing support for combining and grouping conditions in workflow triggers using AND, OR, or a combination of both. Teams can now express complex routing rules, such as (Brand is A or Brand is B) and Priority is Urgent, directly within a single workflow.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

You can now combine multiple conditions within action builder triggers using AND and OR logic, as well as mix both within the same expression. Conditions can also be grouped to represent multi-layered business rules, with support for nesting up to two levels deep.

Specifically, you can:

  • Combine with AND: Require all conditions to be met
  • Combine with OR: Trigger logic when any specified condition is met
  • Mix AND and OR: Combine both types of logic in a single expression
  • Group conditions: Create nested rules (up to two levels) to manage complex routing logic

Why is Zendesk making this change?

When workflows are limited to evaluating a single condition at a time, admins often have to construct almost duplicate flows to cover different scenario variations. By allowing combined and grouped conditions, workflows become simpler to construct and maintain, reducing the total number of steps required to implement your team's business logic.

What do I need to do?

When building or editing a flow in action builder, open a trigger and add your desired conditions. Select how the conditions should be combined, and use grouping to structure your routing rules.

For more information, see Action flow steps and actions reference.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Why do my SMS messages fail to send?
articles.title: Why do my SMS messages fail to send?
articles.body:
Question

Scenario A

I receive one of the error messages below when I send an outbound Text message:

  • We couldn't deliver this message
  • We couldn't send the message
Scenario B

When I review the message details in my Text history, the status of my message is either Undelivered or Failed:

Why are my SMS messages failing?

Answer

Multiple reasons exist for SMS message failure. Common reasons why SMS messages fail to send:

  • The destination handset is unreachable.
  • The destination phone number doesn't support text.
  • The end user sent an opt-out code to one of my messages. For more information on opt-outs, see About opt-out keywords for Zendesk Text.
  • The destination number isn't local and international texting hasn't been enabled. Contact Zendesk Customer Support if you want to enable international texting.
  • The destination number is located in a country where the text number doesn't support SMS long code international messaging. For example, Zendesk US text numbers can't send SMS messages to UK numbers. For more information, see Twilio's SMS guidelines.

If SMS messages still fail to send or if you need your US/CA toll-free numbers verified, contact Zendesk Customer Support with the ticket ID where the SMS message failed for further assistance.

articles.name: Configuring call console access in Contact Center
articles.title: Configuring call console access in Contact Center
articles.body:
Admins can control which team members can use the Contact Center call console. The call console icon () doesn’t display in the workspace of a team member who doesn’t have access.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can limit access to the call console with roles and groups. Team members need at least one selected role and one selected group to use the call console, and if either list is left empty, it won’t restrict access. This helps you manage Contact Center call console access and keep the workspace icon visible only for the right people.

Location: Contact center > Overview

Admins can control which team members can use the Contact Center call console. The call console icon () doesn’t display in the workspace of a team member who doesn’t have access.

To use the call console, team members must configure their browser for calls. For more information, refer your team members to Using the Contact Center agent interface and configuring voice preferences.

To configure call console access

  1. In Contact Center, click Overview.
  2. Access the Call console access section.

    You can restrict call console access to the team members who need it by selecting the Zendesk roles and groups they must belong to. By default, no roles or groups are selected, giving all team members access to the call console.

    Team members must have at least one selected role and belong to at least one selected group to access the call console. If you leave either list empty, that list doesn’t limit access.

    Note: Amazon Connect admins must also assign the team members a security profile with access to the Amazon Connect Contact Control Panel. For more information, see Provide agents with access to the Connect Customer Contact Control Panel (CCP) in Amazon documentation.


  3. Click the Roles menu, then select the roles that can have access to the call console.

    To help find roles, you can search the list by role name. Matching roles appear as you type.

    By default, no role is selected, meaning roles don't limit access.

    When you select roles, a team member must have at least one of the selected roles to access the call console.

  4. Click the Groups menu, then select the groups that can have access to the call console.

    To help find groups, you can search the list by group name. Matching groups appear as you type.

    By default, no group is selected, meaning group membership doesn't limit access.

    When you select groups, a team member must belong to at least one of the selected groups to access the call console.

  5. Click Save.

articles.name: Can the WhatsApp "Message Us" button label be translated into multiple languages?
articles.title: Can the WhatsApp "Message Us" button label be translated into multiple languages?
articles.body:
Question

Can I translate the WhatsApp Message Us button into multiple languages in Zendesk?

Answer

The Message Us button is configured in Zendesk > Admin Center > Channels > Messaging and Social > Messaging. That button currently supports only a single Label field. There is no built-in option to set different label translations per language within that configuration.

To make the button language-aware, replace the hardcoded text with a Zendesk Dynamic Content placeholder. Dynamic content automatically displays the correct language variant based on the end user's detected locale.

Step 1: Create the Dynamic Content Item

  1. In Admin Center, click Workspaces in the sidebar.
  2. Select Agent tools > Dynamic content.
  3. Click Add item.
  4. Enter a descriptive title (e.g., message_us_button_label).
  5. Select your default language and enter the default button label text.
  6. Click Create.

Step 2: Add Language Variants

  1. Open the dynamic content item you just created.
  2. Click Add variant to create versions for each of your supported languages.
  3. Select the target language and enter the translated label text.
  4. Set the variant status to either Active that will display to users viewing the Help Center in that language, or Inactive and users in that language will see the default language variant instead.
  5. Save your changes and copy the generated placeholder code.

Step 3: Update Your HTML Snippet

In the HTML code, replace the hardcoded label value in your iframe snippet with your dynamic content placeholder.

Example snippet: label={{dc 'name_of_your_dynamic_content_with_underscores' }}

Important considerations

  • Fallback language: If an end user's language is not supported or active in your Dynamic Content settings, the system automatically displays your designated default variant.
  • Locale matching: Ensure the language code selected in your dynamic content variant matches the exact locale enabled under Admin Center > Account > Appearance > Languages (for example, English (US) vs. English (UK)).

articles.name: Troubleshooting issues in the new article editor
articles.title: Troubleshooting issues in the new article editor
articles.body:
When you move to the new article editor from the legacy editor, you might notice changes to tables, links, spacing, lists, or headings. Use the sections below to find the issue and try the relevant fix.

Before changing your help center theme or article source code, back up the content or CSS you plan to edit. Preview changes before publishing.

Troubleshooting issues with tables

How to fix a table wrap in <figure> elements

The new article editor uses <figure> tags to provide consistent styles and features for tables across different browsers and platforms. This behavior is part of the new editor's table plugin architecture. It can cause style issues, such as a restricted table height or unwanted format issues. This section explains why this happens and how to prevent or fix it.

Important: Back up your CSS and content before you make major changes.

The new article editor wraps tables in <figure class="table"> elements and may apply inline styles that override custom classes.

To restore your table styles:

  1. Update your CSS selectors to target the new markup:
    • figure.table table { /* your table styles */ }
    • figure.table th, figure.table td { /* cell styles */ }
  2. Use !important sparingly to override inline styles if needed
  3. Test your changes in a duplicate article before you apply them site-wide

To prevent or fix table wrap issues:

  • Review your help center CSS to ensure that <figure class="table"> elements don't have restrictive styles, such as max-height or overflow settings
  • If you see style issues, update your CSS to target <figure class="table"> as shown:
    figure.table {
    max-height: none;
    overflow: visible;
    }
  • If you migrate content, don't remove <figure> tags by hand. The new article editor may add them again when you edit content.
Note: This guidance is based on general product knowledge and is not explicitly present in the original tickets. The new article editor relies on <figure> wrappers by design for feature support and consistency. Use help center CSS customization to resolve style issues, not changes to the editor output HTML.

How to fix table header and header level format issues

Common format issues after migration:

  • Table headers may lose their background color or styles
  • Table header cells may convert incorrectly to H2 text
  • H2, H3 sizes may appear different due to changes in default or custom CSS
  • The editor may not save table changes as expected

To ensure that table headers display correctly after migration:

  1. In your help center theme, add CSS rules that target <thead> or <th> elements, for example:
    thead { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
    th { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
  2. Keep or update any existing <th> styles to maintain consistency

To set table headers in the new article editor:

  1. In the article, select your table, then click the top row
  2. From the Row dropdown, turn on the Header row option
    • If the header row option is missing, manually add <thead> and <th> elements in the HTML source, or check for available plugins or editor options in your new article editor setup

If H2 or H3 styles appear incorrect

Review and update header levels:

  1. Edit the article in the new article editor
  2. Select any table header text that the editor converted to H2
  3. Change its format to the correct style, such as a table header or normal text

Adjust header level sizes with CSS:

  1. Go to Knowledge admin > Customize design > Customize > Edit code > style.css
  2. Update the CSS to ensure that H2, H3, and similar styles match your desired sizes
  3. Use the Preview feature to check the final format before you click Publish

If the editor doesn't save your table changes or you see errors like no changes have been made:

  1. Try to reproduce the issue
  2. Capture an HTTP Archive (HAR) file and a screen capture
  3. Contact Zendesk Customer Support for further help

See

  • Fixing table styling when transitioning to the new article editor
  • Adding and formatting tables in help center articles
Tip: If you have many articles to update, consider a batch script or a migration tool to standardize header levels and styles, and back up your articles every time before you make bulk changes. If your new article editor implementation lacks certain table features, check for available plugins or contact your platform admin for enhancements.

How to fix table format and alignment issues

Common issues after migration:

  • Custom table styles for width and borders do not apply as before
  • Inconsistent text size and cell space
  • Table classes and border styles changed during a migration
  • Header rows split between <thead> and <tbody>, which causes style inconsistencies
  • Text overflow and table border issues

To fix these issues:

  • Update your help center CSS to target table elements
    .article-body td, .article-body th {
    padding: 20px;
    font-size: 16px;
    }
  • Fix table alignment
    • Use the new article editor table alignment options. The new article editor may have fewer features than the legacy editor.
    • If tables center every time or alignment does not work, add or adjust CSS:
      .article-body table {
      margin-left: 0 !important;
      margin-right: auto !important;
      }
  • Manage table cell space and alignment
    • Remove unnecessary inline styles that set cell space so your theme CSS controls that property
    • Define the desired cell space in your theme CSS
  • Adjust table classes, borders, and headers
    • Update CSS rules for any new or changed table classes, for example, .nonItemList
    • Ensure that all header rows are inside <thead> for proper styling
    • Move any header rows from <tbody> to <thead> as needed
  • Table text escapes borders or does not wrap as expected, especially after you add a table border in the article editor
    • Use these help center theme CSS rules to ensure table cell text wracts correctly and stays within the table borders
      /* 1. Target the class name from your table tag */
      table.wysiwyg-table-resized {
      /* This tells the browser: "Do not look at the content to decide width.
      Look at the <col> widths (40%/60%) and obey them strictly." */
      table-layout: fixed;
      width: 100%;
      }

      /* 2. Target the cells to ensure wrapping happens */
      table.wysiwyg-table-resized td {
      /* Forces text to go to the next line when it hits the edge */
      white-space: normal;

      /* Breaks long words/URLs if they are too wide for the 60% column */
      overflow-wrap: break-word;
      word-wrap: break-word;

      /* Optional: Makes reading easier by aligning text to the top */
      vertical-align: top;
      }
  • Articles edited or migrated from earlier versions of Zendesk Guide may contain legacy formatting that conflicts with your current theme CSS. If fixes do not apply as expected, inspect the table’s HTML and remove extra formatting or attributes that may affect layout.
    • In the article editor, select the table and remove any specific width or style settings applied through the article editor table controls
    • If necessary, switch to the HTML view and delete width attributes or inline style tags from <table>, <tr>, or <td> elements
  • Test and verify changes
    • Preview affected articles in the new article editor to confirm the formatting
    • Repeat for each article with custom tables, as a manual review may be required

Troubleshooting issues with links

Immediate workarounds

If you see these issues, switch to the legacy editor.

To do this:

  1. In the Article settings panel, select Switch to legacy editor
  2. Update the hyperlink in the legacy editor
  3. Switch back to the new article editor
  4. When you switch editors, use the feedback prompt to report the issue to the engineering team

If the visual editor does not update links, edit them in HTML:

  1. Open the article in the new article editor
  2. Click the Source code icon on the toolbar
  3. Locate the <a> tag, the anchor for the link you need to edit
  4. Update the URL or link text
  5. To open the link in a new tab, add target="_blank" rel="noopener" to the <a> tag.
    For example: <a href="URL" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Link Text</a>
  6. Save your changes and switch back to the visual editor to confirm the link appears and works as expected

More fixes

  • Update the article editor to the latest version. Check for patches.
  • After you update, clear your browser cache to load the latest editor
  • Edit and insert links to check if the issues are fixed
  • If problems continue, contact your support team or product manager. Include your browser version and steps to show the issue.
  • If you are not sure a fix is live, ask your support contact or check platform announcements
  • If problems remain after updates, clear your cache again or use a different browser to check for browser or cache issues

Troubleshooting formatting issues

Extra spaces and line breaks

To fix this:

  1. Review your articles for extra spaces or blank lines, especially between paragraphs, lists, and headings
  2. Open the article in the new article editor
  3. Click the Source code icon from the toolbar
  4. Remove unnecessary <br> tags or extra spaces, especially inside lists or near headings
  5. Save and preview the article to confirm the issue is resolved

Bullet lists <ul> display as numbered lists

Reason: Your theme CSS overrides the default style.

To fix this:

  1. Go to Knowledge admin > Customize design > Customize > Edit code > style.CSS
  2. Inspect your CSS for rules such as ul { list-style-type: decimal; }
  3. Change or add ul { list-style-type: disc; }
  4. Use the Preview feature to check the final format before you click Publish

Nested and multi-level don’t display correctly

Reason: The new article editor doesn’t natively support mixed-style nested lists. For example, numbers for the first level and letters for the second, in the editor UI.

To fix this, update your theme CSS to create custom nested number styles in published articles.

Add CSS such as:

ol {
    counter-reset: item;
    padding-left: 10px;
  }
  li {
    display: block;
  }
  li:before {
    content: counters(item, ".") " ";
    counter-increment: item;
  }
Tip: Use the Preview feature every time to check the final format before you save and publish.

In the editor, nested lists might show a uniform number style, but the published view restores the correct hierarchy (numbers, letters, Roman numerals). A custom number style might not appear in the editor preview unless you insert CSS in the article source, which isn't recommended for maintenance reasons.

Heading formats go missing or reset after you press Enter

To fix this:

  1. Open the article in the new article editor
  2. Refresh your browser and clear the cache
  3. Contact Zendesk Customer Support for further help.

articles.name: Why doesn't a solved ticket appear in real-time monitoring charts where I expect?
articles.title: Why doesn't a solved ticket appear in real-time monitoring charts where I expect?
articles.body:
Question

I solved or updated a ticket, but why isn't it showing up in the time period I expect on a real-time monitoring report?

Answer

Some real-time charts group ticket activity by when a ticket enters a specific state. For example, charts track when a user creates a ticket or when it enters a queue, rather than when you update or solve it.

An earlier event, rather than the most recent update, generally locks in a ticket's position on the chart. If you solve a ticket today, it doesn't necessarily move into today's bucket on every chart. The chart may measure a different moment in the ticket lifecycle.

A few examples of how this works:

  • Queue activity charts, for example, Standard queue activity for email, track when a ticket entered or exited a specific queue. Solving the ticket later doesn't change when it entered or exited that queue, so it remains in that original time window.
  • Ticket-count and satisfaction charts that use rolling time buckets assign each ticket to the bucket active during ticket creation. They don't assign tickets based on when you update, solve, or rate them. If you solve an older ticket today, the chart still links it to its original creation bucket. The ticket might not appear in a shorter time window that only looks back a few days.
  • Because the system recalculates bucket boundaries every time the dashboard loads, they don't match the ticket creation time. The same ticket can appear in a different bucket on a later view, even when nothing about the ticket changed. For example, an August 16 ticket might appear in the August 15 bucket if the nearest boundary fell at 9:04:55 PM on August 15. This occurs if someone creates the ticket just before the next boundary at 9:04:55 PM on August 16.
  • In some cases, the system finalizes the chart's underlying record after a specific field, such as an end time, receives a value. If that happens before a later status change, the chart won't retroactively reflect that later change.

What this means for you

This is expected behavior, not missing or broken data. The ticket data itself remains intact. However, the chart measures a specific moment in time rather than the most recent update, and bucket boundaries can shift between views.

To confirm a ticket's current status or historical changes, check the ticket itself. You can also report on it using a standard Zendesk Analytics dataset, such as Tickets or Updates history.

Use real-time monitoring charts to track current workload and activity trends, rather than as an audit trail of every status change.

articles.name: Why do real-time monitoring charts show a time or date that hasn't happened yet?
articles.title: Why do real-time monitoring charts show a time or date that hasn't happened yet?
articles.body:
Question

Why do real-time monitoring charts show a time or date that hasn't happened yet?

Answer

This is expected behavior. Real-time monitoring charts don't group data into fixed clock-hour or calendar-day buckets the way a standard historical report does. Instead, they build their time buckets backward from the exact moment you open the dashboard. They set the edge of the most recent bucket to the next upcoming boundary every time, rather than the last one that passed.

This design means the chart's current bucket includes active tickets and tickets with recent updates. The chart does not wait for a boundary to close fully before showing that activity.

The system calculates bucket boundaries in UTC and displays them in your account's local time zone. The label on that final bar can look like it's ahead of "now," especially if your time zone is several hours ahead of UTC.

How the time buckets work

The size of each bucket depends on the reporting window you select:

  • Last 15–120 minutes: 5–30 minutes
  • Last 8–24 hours: 1–3 hours
  • Last 48 hours: 6 hours
  • Last 7 or 14 days: 1 day
  • Last 30 days: 1 day

The system rounds up each bucket boundary to the next clean UTC interval for that bucket size. For an hourly chart, boundaries land on even UTC hours, such as 00:00, 03:00, and 06:00 UTC. For a daily chart, every boundary lands on UTC midnight.

Example: hourly chart that shows a future time

With a 24-hour reporting window, buckets are 3 hours apart and align with UTC. For example, if you view the dashboard at 11:54 AM in a time zone that's UTC+11, that's 12:54 AM UTC. The next 3-hour UTC boundary is 3:00 AM UTC, which displays in your local time zone as 2:00 PM. The latest bar shows this time.

Example: daily chart that shows tomorrow's date

With a 7-day reporting window, buckets are 1 day apart and align with UTC midnight. If you view the dashboard at 12:08 PM 08/10/2026 in a time zone that's UTC+11, that's 1:08 AM UTC. The next UTC midnight is tomorrow at 12:00 AM UTC, which displays in your local time zone as 11:00 AM 09/10/2026 tomorrow's date. The latest bar shows this date.

Does this mean my data is wrong?

No. The ticket counts in each bar are accurate for the window of time that bucket represents. Only the label on the bucket boundary changes. The system recalculates the boundary relative to the moment you load the dashboard, rather than fixing it to your local clock.

If you reload the dashboard, the bucket boundaries shift forward again to match the refreshed time, and the labels update accordingly.

articles.name: Every incoming email sent to my Zendesk is suspended
articles.title: Every incoming email sent to my Zendesk is suspended
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I set up email forwarding from an external support address to my Zendesk and now every email appears on the suspended view.

Causes

The cause of these suspended emails usually is an incorrect set of a web form with email forwarding, a spammy sender, or an issue with email headers and automations. For more information, see Causes for ticket suspension.

Additional suspension causes include:

  • Received from support address indicates that your email server is configured with an external support address, for example, support@example.com, as the From or Reply-To header in every email forwarded to your Zendesk. These messages are suspended by Zendesk due to the ability to cause mail loops. To resolve this issue, modify the email forwarding on your server to show the email address of the ticket requester email address rather than your external support address in the From or Reply-To header.
  • Automated response email indicates that the email server is adding an automated header such as Precedence: bulk or Auto-submitted: auto-generated to every email that is forwarded to your Zendesk account. These headers tell Zendesk that the messages were auto-generated rather than created by end users. To resolve this issue, modify the email forwarding on your server to not add either of these headers to forwarded email messages.

Resolution steps

To avoid all emails being suspended or rejected, follow these steps:

  1. Verify if you use a web form with email. This isn't supported and causes errors. Instead, use the API to generate tickets from forms.
  2. Ensure that your support address doesn't use unsupported aliases or email groups. Instead, use a regular email address.
  3. Ensure that forwarding is set up at the server level, instead of in the individual settings of your email address.
  4. Verify your SPF record.
  5. The email header cannot contain unsupported entries under Automated response from Causes for ticket suspension. For example, Delivered-To, Auto-Submitted, or Autoresponder are not supported.
  6. Don't use an email address that starts with noreply@, daemon@, or postmaster@, as these are not supported.
  7. Verify that the emails do not contain any unsubscribe links, as these are not supported.
  8. Verify that the emails are not automatic replies, as these are not supported.
  9. If after verifying the above, you are still facing issues, further troubleshooting is required. Take a full page screenshot of one example (including the sender, receiver, and time) and share it with Zendesk Customer Support.
Note: If you don't have access to your email server, reach out to your email administrator or email hosting company. Modify your email forwarding in order to resolve issues.

articles.name: Can the Opening line be set for first initial reply only?
articles.title: Can the Opening line be set for first initial reply only?
articles.body:
Question

For Email content in the agentic AI for email, can the Opening line or message be set for first initial reply only?

  • I do not want subsequent replies by the AI agent or bot to surface that greeting
  • For example, my team created an Opening line that says: Greetings and thank you for your email. However, that message keeps appearing on all AI agent back-and-forth conversations, which is not a great experience for my customers.

Answer

No. There is currently no setting to show a custom greeting only in the initial AI reply and suppress it in later follow-ups within the same thread.

For this reason, use an AI-generated greeting instead, which may vary but will feel more conversational:

  1. Remove the current greeting in the Opening line and leave the field blank
  2. In that case, the AI will attempt to create its own context-appropriate opening for each message, but you cannot explicitly limit a custom greeting to just the first reply

articles.name: Why is my AI agent replying in a disabled or unsupported language?
articles.title: Why is my AI agent replying in a disabled or unsupported language?
articles.body:
Question

Why is my AI agent replying in a disabled or unsupported language?

Answer

Your AI agent can reply in an unexpected language when the conversation language is not explicitly set at the start of the interaction.

If the active_language session parameter is empty, the AI agent may rely on language detection and the customer’s most recent message to determine which language to use. In some cases, especially during small talk, generative responses, or fallback behavior, this can result in the AI agent replying in a language that is not enabled or intended for your configuration.

To make AI agent language behavior more predictable, you can set active_language as soon as the conversation starts.

Why this happens

This behavior is most likely when:

  • active_language is not populated at the beginning of the conversation
  • The AI agent is using language detection based on the latest end-user message
  • The customer sends a message in a different language than their expected or configured language
  • The response comes from a fallback or generative flow that infers language from the prompt context

Recommended fix

Configure an action on the Conversation started event to set active_language using a trusted customer language source, such as:

  • A CRM locale field
  • User profile language data
  • Conversation metadata
  • Another mapped customer language attribute

This helps ensure the AI agent responds in the expected language from the first reply onward.

Best practices

  • Set active_language before the AI agent sends its first response
  • Use a language value that matches one of the languages enabled for the AI agent
  • If you store customer locale information in CRM or metadata, map that value during AI agent initialization
  • Use language detection as a fallback only when no reliable language preference is available

For example, if a customer’s profile locale is stored as fr, you can write that value into active_language when the conversation begins. This tells the AI agent to continue the interaction in French instead of inferring the language from later messages.

For more information, see the resources below:
  • Adding and managing supported languages for AI agents
  • Configuring language detection for AI agents

articles.name: Configuring summaries in Contact Center call notifications
articles.title: Configuring summaries in Contact Center call notifications
articles.body:
Zendesk Contact Center can show agents a summary before they accept an incoming call. Configure a custom summary in an Amazon Connect contact flow, or use Copilot to show a ticket summary.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can show agents a call summary before they answer an incoming call by using either a custom contact flow attribute or an AI-generated ticket summary. Custom summaries use the summary_text attribute, while ticket summaries use summary_zendesk_ticket_id and Copilot. The system shows the first available summary source and can help agents understand the caller’s context, recent ticket history, or unresolved issues.

Zendesk Contact Center can show agents a summary before they accept an incoming call. Configure a custom summary in an Amazon Connect contact flow, or use Copilot to show a ticket summary.

Note: Copilot-generated ticket summaries require the Copilot add-on. A custom summary provided by a contact flow doesn't require Copilot.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Understanding summary sources
  • Configuring custom summaries
  • Configuring ticket summaries

For general contact flow attribute setup, see Mapping and displaying Amazon Connect attributes in Contact Center tickets.

For the agent experience, see Reviewing incoming call information.

Understanding summary sources

Contact Center uses the first available source in this order:

  1. Custom summary: If the contact flow sets the summary_text attribute, Contact Center displays its value.
  2. Summary for a specific ticket: If the flow sets summary_zendesk_ticket_id, Contact Center uses a Copilot summary for that ticket.
  3. Summary for the customer's latest unresolved ticket: If the flow doesn't set either summary attribute and Contact Center recognizes the caller's number, it uses a Copilot summary for the customer's most recent unresolved ticket.

If Contact Center doesn't recognize the caller's number, the notification says: "This is a new customer with no previous tickets." If Contact Center recognizes the customer but can't find an unresolved ticket, it displays a message that no previous tickets are available to summarize.

Configuring custom summaries

Set a user-defined contact attribute named summary_text in the Amazon Connect contact flow. Contact Center displays this value as the call summary, ahead of ticket summaries.

To add a custom summary to a contact flow

  1. In Amazon Connect, select Routing > Contact flows.
  2. Select the contact flow to edit.
  3. Add a Set contact attributes block.
  4. Under Set attributes on, select Current contact.
  5. Click Add another attribute.
  6. Under Namespace, select User defined.
  7. Add the key summary_text and enter the summary value.

    For more information, see Set Attributes from Amazon's documentation.

  8. Click Confirm.

  9. Link the new block to your contact flow.
  10. Click Save.
  11. Click Publish.

Configuring ticket summaries

Ticket summaries let Contact Center show a summary from an existing ticket. Turn on ticket summaries before using this source. For steps, see Turning on and configuring AI-generated ticket summaries. You should select internal notes to ensure the summaries include the entire ticket conversation.

To use a specific ticket, ask the customer or configure a custom Lambda function to set a contact attribute named summary_zendesk_ticket_id to the Zendesk ticket ID. Contact Center then uses that ticket to generate the summary.

For more information, see Store a value from a Lambda functions as a contact attribute in Connect Customer from Amazon's documentation.

articles.name: Is there a limit of exports in my Zendesk sales account?
articles.title: Is there a limit of exports in my Zendesk sales account?
articles.body:
Question

Is there a limit of exports in my Zendesk sales account?

Answer

Yes. You can have only one active Smartlist export per user and one full account export per user. You see a notification in the UI showing that another export is in progress.

Smart lists

Each user can have one Smartlist export in progress at a time. The same user must wait for that export to finish before starting another export.

This limitation applies per user, not per account. Multiple users on the same account can each run one Smartlist export simultaneously.

If one export is running, you see "an export is already in progress" message at the bottom of the UI.

Account exports

Account exports are independent of Smartlist exports. An account export can run while a Smartlist export is in progress, and it doesn't block it. When an account export is in progress, you can't run another account export. The button becomes unavailable and shows a message: "Export in progress. You'll be notified when it is completed."

articles.name: What are lead, contact and deal limits in sales?
articles.title: What are lead, contact and deal limits in sales?
articles.body:
Question

What are the lead, contact, and deal limits in Zendesk Sell? How do they appear in the UI?

Answer

The Zendesk Sell product limits are:

  • Leads: 5,000,000
  • Contacts: 2,000,000
  • Deals: 2,000,000

Information about reaching the lead, contact, or deal limit appears in the product UI. You also receive a warning when approaching the limit. This warning appears when leads are created manually or imported, as well as when a contact or deal is converted from a lead.

When you approach the lead limit, you see the warning message: Nearing lead limit You've used almost all of your 4,500,000 leads. Clear some data now to ensure your account keeps running smoothly. We may enforce these limits at any time to protect system performance.

When you reach the lead limit, you see the warning message: Limit reached. You have 5,000,000 leads. To avoid system issues, manage your leads by removing old records. We may delete data if you stay over this limit.

When you reach the deal limit, you see the warning message: Limit reached. You have 2000000 deals. To avoid system issues, manage your deals by removing old records. We may delete data if you stay over this limit.

When you create a contact by converting a lead or adding one manually, you see the warning message: You have 2000000 contacts. To avoid system issues, manage your contacts by removing old records. We may delete data if you stay over this limit.

If you import deals and contacts and reach both limits, you see the warning message: You have reached the contact limit 2000000 contacts and reached the deal limit 2000000 deals. Please clear some data now to ensure your account keeps running smoothly. We may enforce these limits at any time to protect system performance.

An action flow is a user-defined automated workflow. Each action flow consists of an action flow trigger, which initiates the flow, and one or more actions. Action flows can run in response to their configured trigger or be initiated by agents using agent copilot auto assist, and can consist of a combination of Zendesk actions and connector actions for multiple connected systems. After you connect the action builder to an external system, you can incorporate actions related to that system into your workflows. See the Action flow step and actions reference.

This article describes how to connect action builder to the supported external systems so their actions can be used in your action flows.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

Connecting action builder to external systems uses the external system's authentication process and requirements. Those requirements and processes vary by connector. For specific steps for each connector, expand the sections below.

MCP tools

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets admins connect Zendesk to external MCP servers, discover the tools those servers provide, and use those tools as steps in action flows. This extends your Zendesk workflows to interact with third-party systems—such as project management tools, e-commerce platforms, or internal knowledge systems—without building custom API integrations.

MCP server connections are created and managed in Admin Center. After you create a connection, Zendesk retrieves the available MCP tools from that server and displays them in the action builder so you can use them in action flows and, optionally, surface those flows through auto assist, AI agents, or custom agents.

For more information, see Connecting to MCP servers and using MCP tools in action flows.

ServiceNow

  2. Use the OAuth client to connect Workday to the action builder.

    After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Workday.

  3. (Optional) Configure Workday to allow contact information to be updated through REST API requests.
To set up an OAuth 2.0 client in Workday
  1. Sign into your Workday account as an administrator.
  2. In the Workday search bar, type Edit Tenant Setup - Security, then select the matching option from the search results list.
  3. Scroll down to the OAuth 2.0 Settings section and turn on the OAuth 2.0 configuration.
  4. Configure the API client:
    • Search: Select Register API Client.
    • Client Name: Enter a meaningful name for your client, such as Zendesk connection.
    • Client Grant Type: Choose Authorization Code. See OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice for more information about grant types.
    • Client Redirect URL: Enter

      https://zis.zendesk.com/api/services/zis/connections/oauth/callback

  5. Use the API scopes field to specify the following permissions for the app to access Workday data:

    • Staffing
    • Time off and leave

    • Client Secret

    • Token Endpoint URL
    • Authorization Endpoint URL
    • Workday REST API URL

    • Workday REST API URL

  7. Follow Workday's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.

articles.body:
If a ticket remains unassigned to a group for more than an hour, I'd like to create an automation to assign it to a default group. Also, how can I exclude AI agents from the conditions for those tickets?

The workflow includes the steps below.

Step 1: Check for ticket tags

First, ensure that your AI agent workflow adds this dedicated tag to tickets: handled_by_ai_agent. Add that tag immediately through the AI integration.

Step 2: Create a fallback automation

Create a fallback automation with at least four Meet all conditions:

  • Ticket: Group | Is | -
  • Ticket: Status category | Less than | Solved
  • Ticket: Hours since created | Greater than | 1

  • Ticket: Tags | Contains none of the following | handled_by_ai_agent auto_assigned_default_group

Step 3: Add actions

In your automation, add the following actions:

  • Ticket: Group | select your default group

  • Ticket: Add tags | auto_assigned_default_group

Step 4: Create a test ticket

After one to two hours, verify that the automation appears in the ticket events. This gives enough time for the automation to run.

articles.name: Announcing an EAP for the agentic shopping assistant, as part of the commerce agent
articles.title: Announcing an EAP for the agentic shopping assistant, as part of the commerce agent
articles.body:
We are excited to introduce an early access program (EAP) for the agentic shopping assistant, part of a commerce agent, that reaches out to buyers at the right time, offering a personalized buying experience based on their customer context.

This announcement answers the following questions:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

The agentic shopping assistant enables businesses to provide personalized shopping assistance directly to their customers. Key features included in this EAP are:

  • Proactive messaging: Instead of waiting for shoppers to discover the shopping assistant, proactive messaging engages shoppers at the right moment. 
  • Personalized product discovery: The agent understands buyer intent and offers personalized product discovery. 
  • Evaluation and product Q&A: It also supports product evaluation by answering product Q&A and facilitating product comparisons.
  • Unified reporting and monitoring: Businesses get insights into how the shopping assistant is performing through reporting , allowing admins to analyze user progress and abandonment across buyer journey stages. Supervisors can also view active AI agent conversations in real time.

For more information, see Using an agentic shopping assistant to proactively assist buyers on Shopify storefronts (EAP).

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Currently, the buyer needs to navigate through the website to discover products, evaluate them by reading through the product description, and then complete purchases.

We believe that the buying experience needs to be proactive, personalized, and contextual based on the stage of their buying journey.

What do I need to do?

To participate in the EAP, your account must meet the following criteria:

  • Messaging and AI agents: You must have messaging set up and be using AI agents.
  • Shopify integration: You must have connected your Shopify storefront to Zendesk.
  • Live monitoring opt-in: You must be opted into the AI agents monitoring EAP for live monitoring of commerce conversations.
  • Reporting opt-in: You must be opted into the agentic analytics EAP to enable reporting on conversations handled by the shopping assistant.

If you meet the requirements above, you can indicate your interest in the EAP by submitting this form. Note that, subject to availability, not every customer who signs up is guaranteed to be included in the EAP, even if you meet the requirements.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: How can I use Google Sheets actions in action flows to search more than 5,000 rows?
articles.title: How can I use Google Sheets actions in action flows to search more than 5,000 rows?
articles.body:
Question

Can I use the Google Sheets Search rows action in action flows if it returns more than 5,000 rows?

Answer

Yes, you can configure the Google Sheets Search rows action to search the content of sheets with more than 5,000 rows. To achieve this, you must increase the row count.

How to increase the row count returned per page on Search rows

  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Click the name of an existing action flow to open it or click Create flow to create a new action flow.
  3. In the action builder, click the Add step icon ().
  4. In the step sidebar, under Connected, click Google Sheets and then select Search rows.
  5. Configure the step.
  6. Under Additional fields, select Row count and enter 5000. The row count value determines how many rows can be returned on the first page.
  7. If there are more than 5,000 search results, use the Page token returned in the response to retrieve the next page of results.
  8. Finish creating or updating the action flow as needed, and then click Save.

For more information, see these articles:

  • Creating action flows
  • Using Google Sheet actions in action flows

articles.name: Service Incident - September 21, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Multiple customers in the DACH region are seeing SMTP 554 rejections when sending ticket replies
articles.title: Service Incident - September 21, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Multiple customers in the DACH region are seeing SMTP 554 rejections when sending ticket replies
articles.body:
Summary

Between 07:50 UTC and 14:30 UTC on 21 September 2026, Support customers in the DACH region experienced delivery failures when sending outbound ticket replies to recipients using GMX, web.de, IONOS/1&1, and mail.com email addresses. Affected messages received permanent SMTP 554 rejection responses and were neither delivered nor automatically retried.

Timeline

September 21, 2026 14:09 UTC | September 21, 2026 7:09 AM PT

We are aware of an issue impacting outbound email delivery to some mail providers. Some outbound email may fail with an error code 554 -- permanent rejection, meaning the outbound email was not sent and will not be retried. We are working with these mail providers and will provide an update as soon as possible.

September 21, 2026 14:50 UTC | September 21, 2026 7:50 AM PT

We have observed recovery and are now seeing successful outbound email delivery to the affected email providers. Please let us know if you continue to see any 554 status coded rejections to these recipients. Unfortunately we are unable to resend these emails on your behalf, and we apologize for that inconvenience.

September 21, 2026 15:01 UTC | September 21, 2026 8:01 AM PT

We are no longer seeing any email rejections to the providers that were rejecting emails sent via Zendesk. We do apologize for the disruption in your ability to send outbound mail during this incident. You will find any failed outbound emails in each of the respective tickets (reference). Unfortunately we are unable to resend them on your behalf, so adding another public comment to send a new outbound email will be required.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by United Internet applying an email block to mail sent from the broader zendesk.com domain. The intended scope of the block was limited to a single subdomain, following a high volume of email traffic from that source.

Because the block was applied at the broader domain level, it also affected legitimate ticket reply emails sent from other zendesk.com addresses.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we submitted removal requests through the affected email providers’ support channels. United Internet then corrected the overly broad block. Outbound email delivery recovered, and SMTP 554 rejection responses stopped.

Remediation Items

  1. Develop a scalable process to identify and block abusive email activity more quickly.
  2. Define a controlled approach for gradually increasing outbound email volumes for new or high-volume customers.
  3. Introduce outbound email sending limits for new and trial accounts to reduce the risk of excessive sending activity.
  4. Improve customer self-service options for recovering ticket reply emails that are permanently rejected.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.title: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.body:
Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can let agents choose an outbound queue for calls, which controls the caller ID shown to recipients and the flow that handles the call. You can allow access to all queues or only queues tied to the agent’s routing profile. This helps you manage outbound call routing and queue selection, but calls from queues without an outbound number will fail.

Location: Contact Center > Routing > Outbound calls.

Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

For information about configuring routing profiles and their queues, see Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center. For the agent procedure, see Selecting the outbound queue for a call.

To turn on outbound queue selection

  1. In Contact Center, click Routing > Outbound calls.

  2. Select Allow agents to select an outbound queue.
  3. Select the queues that agents can access:
    • All queues: Agents can place a call from any queue, regardless of their Amazon Connect routing profile.
    • All queues associated with the agent's routing profile: Agents can place a call only from queues associated with their Amazon Connect routing profile.
    Note: Queues appear to agents even if they don't have an outbound number. Calls placed using those queues fail.
  4. Click Save.

    Agents can now select one of the available queues when placing an outbound call.

articles.name: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.title: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.body:
A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can update an Amazon Connect routing profile to control which queues agents handle, set queue priority and delay, and limit concurrent contacts. This helps you manage agent capacity and set the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls. If you turn on outbound queue selection, agents can choose an outbound queue for calls.

A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

Each agent has one routing profile. To let agents choose an outbound queue, turn on outbound queue selection in Contact Center. For more information, see Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center.

For more information about creating routing profiles and linking queues to agents, see Create a routing profile in Amazon Connect to link queues to agents in the AWS documentation.

To update a routing profile

  1. In Amazon Connect, click Users > Routing profiles.
  2. Click the routing profile you want to edit.
  3. Update the channels, queues, and concurrency settings as needed.

  4. Click Save.

articles.name: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.title: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I try to sign in to Zendesk, I see the error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error.

In the browser console and network logs, I may see 5xx errors.

Resolution steps

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause this error. Confirm whether affected agents still see the error when they connect from a device that doesn’t use these tools.

If users still have issues, contact Zendesk Customer Support and include an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from one affected user.

Why do I see "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"? How do I fix "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error" when signing in? What causes "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"?

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause 5xx errors in browser console and network logs.

To resolve this error, follow these steps:

  1. Connect to your Zendesk help desk or ticketing system from a device that does not use VPN or antivirus tools.
  2. Check if the error disappears.
  3. If you still see the error, contact Zendesk Customer Support.
  4. Provide an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from an affected support person or agent.

articles.name: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.title: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.body:
Summary

Between 14:26 UTC and 17:40 UTC on 17 September 2026, Voice customers on Pod 20 experienced an issue that caused some agents to remain in wrap-up mode after calls. Affected agents were not offered new incoming calls, which could delay inbound call handling.

Timeline

September 17, 2026 16:53 UTC | September 17, 2026 9:53 AM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting Voice on Pod 20 that is causing agents to experience difficulties leaving wrap-up mode. We are also seeing some call recordings not appended to tickets as expected. We are investigating and will provide further information when we have a substantive update to share. In the meantime, we recommend trying to manually click "finish wrap-up" (don't wait for the auto-timeout), and in case "finish wrap-up" doesn't respond, toggle Voice availability Off then On. Please let us know if the issue persists after attempting the workaround. Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

September 17, 2026 18:25 UTC | September 17, 2026 11:25 AM PT

Our team has addressed the underlying cause of the issue that prevented some agents from exiting wrap-up mode after a Voice call.  Agents ending a call should see wrap-up, and all relevant agent availability functions are back to normal. Thank you for your patience while we recovered from this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a high volume of duplicate agent availability updates generated by a single Voice session. Because the service did not adequately prevent duplicate requests or limit repeated updates from an individual agent, the traffic overwhelmed shared processing capacity on Pod 20 and delayed lower-priority work.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we temporarily disabled the affected account’s embedded calling feature to stop further repeated availability updates. We then allowed pending work to be processed and re-enabled the feature after system performance had stabilized.

Remediation Items

  1. Introduce limits on how frequently an individual user can submit availability updates.
  2. Add a controlled way to immediately pause embedded calling updates when abnormal activity is detected.
  3. Separate availability checks from the primary system responsible for saving updates, reducing pressure on critical services.
  4. Apply stricter safeguards to prevent excessive or repeated availability changes from being processed.
  5. Prioritize the work required to return agents to an available state after a call, reducing the likelihood of delayed incoming call handling.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.title: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents. My company provides customer support for other organizations. Because of this, I use 1 web crawler per organization that I support.

The problem is there is a limit of 50 web crawlers for each AI agent. I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations, but we are unable to import any knowledge from said organizations due to the limit on web crawlers. Do you have advice on a workaround or re-architecting this build with best practices?

Resolution steps

Firstly, the web crawler does not have a limit for each AI agent, but for each Zendesk account.

  • Consider reaching out to your sales team at Zendesk to ask for an alternative.

In addition, if your team has developer and engineering resources, you may be interested to make use of the Federated Search API concept and these 2 methods:

  • The Web crawler lets your team implement federated search in your help center without developer resources. Set up multiple crawlers in your help center search settings to crawl and index different content in the same or different websites.
  • The Federated Search API allows developers to build custom integrations and ingest external content records into your Zendesk search indexes. This API requires your developers to build and maintain a middleware layer and integrate the site that hosts the external content with the help center. External records ingested through the Federated Search API refresh based on your configuration, whereas web crawlers run based on your selected refresh schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, or never) or can be triggered manually.

articles.name: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.title: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am using CSV knowledge and AI agents - Advanced (legacy). After installing the CSV Knowledge Importer, I can't get the AI Agent to pull from my CSV knowledge. No matter what question I am asking the AI agents for information from the CSV knowledge source, my bot simply goes to the default reply.

This is what I've done:

  • I have installed and added the CSV knowledge importer.
  • I have ensured the CSV knowledge is added as a knowledge source in AI Agents.
  • I then tried to ask the bot a very simple question from something I knew was in the CSV knowledge source.

Root cause

The Knowledge Reply use case may be restricted to articles from a Recommendation search rule.

Resolution steps

To solve this issue:

  1. Remove any Recommendation search restriction from your use case
  2. Ensure your Intent shows Generative replies > Response generated
  3. Publish your updated configuration
  4. Refresh the page or clear your cache and cookies, and the Knowledge sources should return replies
